images.name: burst-pipe
images.prompt:
A wall opened in two places along its length, exposing wet framing and insulation inside both cavities, with a thermal camera resting on a step stool in the foreground pointed at the wall. A copper pipe is visible in the further opening. Cut sections of drywall lean against the opposite wall. Dust and fragments across the floor.

Shot by a restoration technician on a mid-range phone during the job — a working record, not a photograph anyone meant to be seen.
No people. No hands. No technicians. Nobody in frame. But it should look actively worked: tools set down mid-task, materials pulled apart and left where they fell, equipment running.
LIGHT: whatever was already there. An overhead fixture, grey daylight, or a work light. Mixed colour temperature is fine. No sun shafts, no golden hour, no backlighting, no bright highlights, no blown-out areas.
SURFACES: everything has history. Paint has roller texture and patched spots that do not match. Timber is marked and inconsistent. Carpet shows traffic lanes and uneven pile. Dust in corners, untidy cable runs, chipped baseboards. Nothing repeats cleanly across the frame.
CAMERA: handheld, slightly off-level, imperfect framing with something clipped at an edge. Natural phone depth of field. Visible sensor noise in darker areas. Flat, slightly muted colour as a phone JPEG renders it, not graded.
DO NOT PRODUCE: staged or symmetrical composition; evenly lit studio lighting; glossy surfaces; anything that looks recently renovated; saturated or teal-and-orange colour; shallow depth of field with blurred background; lens flare; bokeh; brand logos; readable text; any person or body part; HDR-looking shadow lift.
If it looks like a product shot or a stock photo, it is wrong. It should look like evidence. 4:3 landscape.

images.name: crawlspace
images.prompt:
Looking into a crawlspace from the access hatch. Wet insulation batts have been pulled down from between the joists and lie in a heap on the vapour barrier. A dehumidifier hose runs in through the opening. A work light on the ground lights the joists above, which show dark staining across the sheeting.
